title: Adaptive token and interactive component cross-engine audit (Safari/Firefox/mobile)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Audit and triage work to resolve cross-engine visual/interaction regressions introduced by recent token scaling and compact mode changes. Scope: tokens, primary/secondary buttons, responsive table layouts with sticky headers, and chart rendering artifacts across Safari (iOS/macOS) and Firefox (desktop). Goal is to produce a prioritized bug list, add reproducible test cases, and land critical fixes or compensating styles before the scheduled UI Kit patch release.
acceptance_criteria: Complete triage for all discovered cross-engine issues and assign owner/estimate
Repro steps and visual regression snapshots added for each bug in Percy/Chromatic or equivalent
Critical regressions (high customer impact) have fixes merged or workaround CSS applied
Design tokens that cause layout regressions have a documented rollback plan or variable override
Add at least 6 automated visual regressions covering affected breakpoints and browsers
Console and SDK consumers confirmed no API contract changes required for the fixes
affected_components: Primary and secondary button variants (compact, icon-only)
Responsive table with sticky header and horizontal scroll
Line and area charts (canvas/svg) with transform-based animations
steps_to_reproduce_examples: Buttons: set density token to --space-scale-compact and open component playground in iOS Safari; note truncated hit area on primary button when icon present
Tables: open large dataset example in Firefox desktop, reduce viewport to 360px width and scroll horizontally; observe sticky header misalignment and double-scroll behavior
Charts: load time-series example in Firefox with reduced motion off; pan chart quickly and observe flicker / aliasing on line path
Tokens: toggle global token set via theme switcher; verify that table cell padding collapses on Safari iOS due to subpixel rounding
